contributions.statement: If the harness orders acceptance checks as a dependency graph and skips children of failed parents, block a child only when its parent mostly fails (here when fewer than 50% of the parent's sub-criteria pass), not on any parent failure. On identical outputs, strict blocking under-counted passing work by 3.4-9.9 pp (mean 6.0) versus 0.6 pp for the soft rule. Do not assume that root-cause-only feedback beats sending the full failure list.
contributions.evidence: App. A Table 2: a same-output re-scoring across 13 model-framework configurations isolates the blocking threshold. Table 3 (DAG vs Flat feedback) compares runs from different paper versions, and Flat had higher project completion for 3 of 4 models, so the feedback-focus benefit is not shown. Frontend web tasks; GPT-5.4 browser judge whose failure detection is not validated (RQ3); one run per cell.
relative_to: 2608.00267 (keep earlier units' acceptance tests as regression obligations)

contributions.statement: Expect edge-case and invalid-input acceptance criteria to be the weakest category for every model even after three feedback rounds (42-88% vs 68-98% for presence checks), so write those criteria explicitly into the spec rather than relying on iteration to surface them.
contributions.evidence: App. D Table 4: the Presence > Functionality > Robustness order holds in all 13 configurations, and the spread widens to 45 pp on Robustness. Self-built benchmark graded by the authors' own GPT-5.4 judge; frontend only; no CIs per type.
relative_to: 2605.15846 (give every spec target its own acceptance test)

contributions.statement: A vague one-line request costs 9-18 pp of first-attempt pass rate against the same agent given a structured requirements document that spells out exception-handling rules, so put acceptance and failure rules into the spec before the first agent run.
contributions.evidence: §5 RQ1, Fig. 5: six models on Claude Code, single run, no CI for this contrast. The hidden criteria are generated from the same PRD, so the PRD arm partly measures being handed the oracle's source.

reason: The benchmark mainly ranks models on frontend tasks. Its mechanism claims (deferring clarification to feedback, DAG feedback improving repair, decoupled repair ability) do not survive the paper's own numbers. The only isolated measurement is the same-output strict-vs-soft blocking gap, which is a narrow evaluator-design point, and the PRD-vs-vague gap restates known ambiguity costs. Nothing here should back a gate.
